newsitem.title: USA: US budget pact should help keep rates low-Sperling.
newsitem.headline: US budget pact should help keep rates low-Sperling.

text.p: The newly reached U.S. budget deal should help keep a lid on long-term interest rates and thus keep the country's economic expansion on track, senior White House official Gene Sperling said on Tuesday.

"I think with this deficit reduction plan...these lower rates will stay and we can continue with the type of investment-led expansion that we've had," Sperlin, who heads the White House's National Economic Council, told Reuters Financial Television.
The agreement between Congressional Republicans and the Clinton administration aims to balance the $1.5 trillion budget by the year 2002 -- for the first time since 1969.
The White House had warned repeatedly that interest rates were likely to go up if the two sides failed to reach a deal.
Long-term U.S. interest rates are now at their lowest level since last December.

"In 1993, we had very high interest rates. When we had the President's powerful 1993 deficit reduction plan, long-term interest rates dropped. They've been pretty low for the last four years," Sperling said.
"I feared...that positive expectations in the market could be taken out and that could see interest rates rise," he added.
Sperling said if the U.S. economy continued to expand at its current pace, gross domestic product could grow over three percent for the year.

"If we have still solid expansion for the rest of the year, you'll see growth for the year of well over three percent," he said, adding that the 2.2 percent growth rate assumed in the budget deal was a "most conservative" estimate. ((-Washington newsroom 202-898 8300))
